note: Living competitor matrix for MONTE WO. Research is batched (quarterly or on major competitor releases) — never crawled continuously. Every entry records its source links and research date. 'verified' = confirmed from official pages/listings; 'reviewer-opinion' = credible third-party reviews; 'marketing' = vendor claims not independently verified.
researchCadence: quarterly + on major competitor release notes

competitors.name: Hevy

setRecording.speed: verified: every set is ~2 taps (weight, reps); previous session values prefilled on the logging screen; automatic rest timer starts when a set is marked complete

competitors.nextActionClarity: verified: rest timer notifies next set; last session's weights visible inline
competitors.onboarding: reviewer-opinion: start with empty workout or routine; low friction
competitors.oneRmProgressionHistory: verified: per-exercise graphs, PR notifications, warm-up calculator (Pro); 1RM charts per exercise
competitors.ranking: verified: exercise leaderboards (social/gym-based, not standards-based); no verification of claims
competitors.offline: reviewer-opinion: works offline, syncs when connected (not stated on official features page)
competitors.accessibility: unknown — not documented on official pages
competitors.freeTier: verified: unlimited workout logging free; 4 routines, 7 custom exercises, 3 months of advanced history; Pro $2.99-$3.99/mo, $23.99/yr, $74.99 lifetime; 150-set cap per workout even on Pro
competitors.privacy: verified: social feed is core (friends, shared workouts); account-based

competitors.name: Strong

setRecording.speed: reviewer-opinion: 'arguably the fastest and most intuitive on the market' (strive-workout.com); supersets supported with older UI (aitoolsbakery)

competitors.nextActionClarity: verified: rest timer; plate calculator and warm-up calculator are Pro-gated
competitors.onboarding: verified: free forever account; unlimited workouts from day one
competitors.oneRmProgressionHistory: verified: 1RM calculator free (per RepReturn); full charts Pro-gated; CSV export; history never locked ('will never be locked out' of data)
competitors.offline: reviewer-opinion: workouts stored locally, sync to iCloud/Google when connected — 'reliable in gyms with poor cell service' (RepReturn)
competitors.freeTier: verified: unlimited logging free; 3 routine cap; PRO $4.99/mo, $29.99/yr, $99.99 lifetime
competitors.privacy: verified: no social feed; account sync optional

competitors.name: Boostcamp

setRecording.speed: verified: full tracker free — RPE/RIR on every set, native supersets and drop sets, plate calculator (10 free uses)

competitors.nextActionClarity: verified: 'every workout laid out for you, with the progression already written in'; Auto Progression (weight targets adjusting to performance) is Pro
competitors.onboarding: verified: program finder by goal/level/equipment/days; beginner defaults named (GZCLP, 5/3/1 for Beginners)
competitors.oneRmProgressionHistory: verified: PRs flagged live, estimated 1RMs free; advanced analytics Pro
competitors.ranking: verified: Strength Score 0-100 DOTS-based across 5 movement patterns — free view; Level/Max/Balance views Pro. Score is self-reported input, not verified lifts
competitors.freeTier: verified: 14,000+ programs free (130+ coach-designed mostly free), unlimited custom program builder, no ads, no time limit; Pro $59.99/yr or $14.99/mo
competitors.privacy: marketing: 'no ads' confirmed free; data practices not reviewed

competitors.name: StrengthLog

setRecording.speed: verified: automatic set-timer; import sets/weights/reps from previous workouts; RPE/RiR optional with auto 1RM calculation

competitors.nextActionClarity: verified: quick-stats while training (rep-PR at this weight? usual reps at this weight?); progression decisions remain with the lifter (reviewer-opinion: gap for lifters who need the app to decide — SteelRep)
competitors.onboarding: verified: free logging from day one, no ads
competitors.oneRmProgressionHistory: verified: 1RM estimate + suggested PR warm-ups free; IPF/Wilks points and Sinclair calculators free
competitors.ranking: verified: IPF/Wilks + Sinclair coefficient calculators — transparent, federation-standard formulas, but self-entered numbers (not verified lifts)
competitors.freeTier: verified: 'most generous free tier' — unlimited workouts, unlimited routines, 450-500+ exercises, basic programs, calculators, no ads; Premium (annual, ~$16.90/mo equiv per SteelRep / $89.95-109/yr per reviews) adds advanced programs + analytics
competitors.privacy: verified: no ads, no social feed; Health Connect/Apple Health integration optional

competitors.name: StrongLifts 5x5

setRecording.speed: verified: log sets from the rest-timer notification via long-press — phone stays locked; watch app logs full workouts

competitors.nextActionClarity: verified: plans every exercise, set and weight; auto-progression +2.5kg/5kg with deload after 3 failures; zero decisions required
competitors.onboarding: verified: starts light, guided; subscription required after trial
competitors.oneRmProgressionHistory: verified: progress graphs, history; warm-up and plate calculators built in
competitors.offline: reviewer-opinion: works fully offline (Lift5x5 comparison); not confirmed on official page
competitors.freeTier: verified: free to download but REQUIRES A SUBSCRIPTION TO USE (own App/Play Store listing): $11.99/mo, $59.99/yr or $199.99 lifetime; 7-day trial only on yearly plan; reviewer-opinion + user reports: history access tied to active subscription

competitors.name: OpenPowerlifting (ranking platform reference)

ranking.model: verified: percentile tiers over judged competition results — intermediate = median competitor, advanced = top 20%, elite = top 5%, world class = top 1% per weight class; data CC0 public domain; 3.5M+ meet entries, 500k+ lifters, 100+ federations
ranking.fairness: verified: every lift performed in public to a defined standard with judges and official weigh-ins; federations filterable; equipment categories kept separate
ranking.contrast: verified: self-reported standards (e.g. Strength Level, 195M+ community-submitted lifts since 2015) run higher than judged-meet data; credible sites (FitnessVolt) keep verified and self-reported populations strictly separate and label both

competitors.lessonsForMonteWo: verified: (1) percentile-of-verified-data is the understandable standard model; (2) never blend verified and self-reported numbers; (3) publish the method — OpenPowerlifting's acceptance comes from open data + open method

monteWoRecommendations.recommendation: Set recording must stay minimal-tap with previous performance visible
monteWoRecommendations.lesson: Hevy's 2-tap logging with prefilled previous values is the category bar; StrongLifts logs from notifications
monteWoRecommendations.fitsMonteWo: Recording a verified performance is our core loop — fewer taps means more complete evidence
monteWoRecommendations.evidenceLabel: verified (official docs) + reviewer-opinion on relative ranking

monteWoRecommendations.recommendation: Show the athlete exactly what to do next (next set, next weight, next verification step)
monteWoRecommendations.lesson: StrongLifts and Boostcamp remove decisions; StrengthLog leaves progression to the lifter and reviewers call it a gap for many users
monteWoRecommendations.fitsMonteWo: Next-action clarity is already our intelligence-system philosophy (agent nextAction) — apply the same to athlete-facing flows

monteWoRecommendations.recommendation: Never lock an athlete's history or verification evidence behind payment
monteWoRecommendations.lesson: StrongLifts' subscription-to-use model and reported history lock-in is the single most-cited trust damage in reviews; Strong explicitly promises the opposite
monteWoRecommendations.fitsMonteWo: Ranks are effort-earned; the record of that effort must remain accessible. Free tier keeps full personal history

monteWoRecommendations.recommendation: Keep provisional / estimated / verified strength results visually and semantically distinct
monteWoRecommendations.lesson: FitnessVolt and OpenPowerlifting-derived sites never blend judged-meet data with self-reported data and label both with source and sample size
monteWoRecommendations.fitsMonteWo: Already our standard — competitor practice confirms it is the credible model; estimated 1RM never displays as a verified rank

monteWoRecommendations.recommendation: Design for offline and low-bandwidth first (local storage, sync when connected, small payloads)
monteWoRecommendations.lesson: Strong stores workouts locally and syncs when connected; reviewers highlight reliability in poor-signal gyms
monteWoRecommendations.fitsMonteWo: Our athletes train where connectivity is unreliable; ETag/304 caching and local-first storage are already TITAN backlog items

monteWoRecommendations.recommendation: A generous free tier is a viable long-term position
monteWoRecommendations.lesson: StrengthLog ('most generous free tier', no ads) and Boostcamp (14,000+ free programs) built loyal user bases on generosity; StrongLifts' hard paywall drove an exodus to alternatives
monteWoRecommendations.fitsMonteWo: Aligned with our $0-budget, free-access mission; monetization (if ever) must not touch rank verification or personal history
monteWoRecommendations.evidenceLabel: verified free-tier facts + reviewer-opinion on outcomes

excludedFromEmulation: Social feeds and gym leaderboards (Hevy): unverified claims + social pressure conflict with effort-earned, verified ranks
AI-generated adaptive programming (Fitbod, Jefit): high operating cost, unauditable recommendations; conflicts with $0 budget and transparent standards
Program marketplaces with paid exclusives (Boostcamp Pro programs): not our model — our standards are open and published
